background: Two-time Coach of the Year (2009 Cleveland, 2023 Sacramento, the latter unanimous) and now a champion head coach after leading the Knicks to the 2026 NBA title in his first season in New York, the franchise's first since 1973. Brown rose through the Spurs' and Pacers' staffs, coached LeBron James's Cavaliers to the 2007 Finals and a 272-138 record (2005-10), had short Lakers stints (2011-13) and a second Cavs year (2013-14), then spent six seasons as Steve Kerr's lead assistant in Golden State (three titles; 11-0 as acting head coach in the 2017 playoffs). In Sacramento (2022-Dec 2024) he installed the fastest-paced, highest-rated offense in league history to that point and ended a 16-year playoff drought before being fired on Dec 27, 2024 after a run of close losses. In New York he replaced Tom Thibodeau, deepened the rotation, pushed three-point volume from 28th to 1st in attempt rate, installed a multi-scheme defense with Darren Erman, and won the championship (53-29, beat ATL, PHI, CLE and SAS 4-1).

evidence: Opening night 2025-26: Knicks used 11 players and six bench players logged at least eight minutes - 'a clear departure' from Thibodeau's eight-man rotation in which all five starters averaged 35+ mpg.
SI: 'minutes balance expected to persist' as a key storyline; Brown praised for 'pulling an anti-Thibs' with bench usage in the 2026 playoffs.
Brunson's time of possession and minutes dropped from Thibodeau's 35.4 mpg; Brown explicitly set out to reduce starter loads.
In Sacramento, Sabonis played all 82 games at roughly 35 mpg and Fox carried heavy minutes, so Brown is not a strict minutes-capper by nature.
Brown 'experimented with lineups incorporating more bench players' throughout 2025-26; criticized after playoff Game 3 vs Atlanta for bench lineups without a primary ball handler.
Sacramento starting lineups were stable, but Knicks bench combinations churned.
Second-year pros (Kolek, Dadiet, Hukporti) cracked the rotation only sporadically; Brown 'doesn't hand out minutes freely'.
In Sacramento he started rookie Keegan Murray for 80 games in 2022-23 (background knowledge).

Managed Mitchell Robinson's workload with minutes restrictions early in 2025-26 (18 minutes vs Miami) but has not been a frequent rester of healthy stars; Sabonis played every game under him in Sacramento.
Closed with matchup pieces (Hart vs Robinson vs Shamet/McBride) during the 2026 run and was credited with tactical lineup adjustments against Atlanta, unlike Thibodeau's fixed closers.
Core closers (Brunson, Towns, Bridges, Anunoby) remained constant.
Kings were No. 1 in pace in 2022-23 under Brown; Knicks moved from 26th to 20th in pace in 2025-26 (Opta Analyst).
Early 2025-26 reporting still called the Knicks a 'slog at times' with bottom-10 pace through seven games - pace is an aspiration more than a constant.
Knicks went from 28th to 1st in three-point attempt rate under Brown (2025-26); 42.9 3PA per game (2nd in NBA) vs 34.1 (26th) under Thibodeau.
Kings under Brown also ranked top-10 in 3PA (background knowledge).

Handoff rates for Towns and Brunson more than doubled; McBride: 'Last year, at times, we got stagnant and we depended on a lot of isolation shots'; Knicks were bottom-eight in passes per possession under Thibodeau.
Finals Games 1-2 featured 295 and 301 passes, the team's best ball movement of the season, before 'old habits' returned in Game 3 (CBS).
Brown's Kings were the league's fastest team and ran off every rebound; in New York he 'aimed for a faster offense' and lifted pace six spots, though the roster is half-court oriented.

Mitchell Robinson remained an elite offensive rebounder in Brown's system and Towns/Hart crash; Sacramento's Sabonis-led teams were middling on the offensive glass (background knowledge; no team rank retrieved).
Offense runs through a hub big (Sabonis in SAC, Towns in NYK) at the elbows/handoffs with some Towns post-ups, but the shot profile is three-heavy rather than paint-first.
Towns 'has been asked to make the biggest adjustment' moving from post/iso toward handoff and spacing roles (ESPN).
Designed the record-setting 2022-23 Kings offense; NBA.com film study credited his in-season 'opportunity for adjustments'; Knicks offense was 'more dynamic' from day one (CBS).
Historically a defense-first coach whose offenses were criticized in Cleveland and LA; modern reputation is markedly improved.
Knicks 'leaned heavily on higher coverages throughout the season rather than playing drop' with Towns at the level, plus switch-heavy and box-and-one looks (Shax, 2025-26).
Sacramento defenses under Brown were conservative and bottom-half; aggressiveness is personnel-driven.

Shifting Towns from deep drop to level coverage prioritizes contesting ball-handlers and shooters at the cost of rim protection; analysts warned level coverage 'invites open threes' when rotations lag.
Thibodeau-era Knicks were a deep-drop, paint-first team; reporting in Jan 2026 noted inconsistency between drop and at-the-level assignments.
No team-level opponent free-throw-rate data retrieved; Brown's teams have generally been average-to-good at avoiding fouls while he himself is frequently fined for officiating complaints (inferred).
Preseason reporting: defensive coordinator Darren Erman 'introduced more zone concepts and switch-heavy alignments'; VSiN: Brown 'ran multi-scheme defense: drop, switch, zone, box+1'.
Brown's Kings were among the league's more frequent zone users (background knowledge).

Explicitly multi-scheme (drop, switch, zone, box-and-one) and changed Towns' base coverage during the season; credited with 'tactical adjustments that have paid dividends' in the 2026 playoffs vs Atlanta.
Midseason (Jan 2026) Ian Begley reported players 'still aren't adjusting' to Brown's tactics, so the scheme variety had an adoption cost.
Brown is an emotional, engaged sideline presence who is quick to confront officials and stop play; no systematic data on timeout timing found (inferred).
No direct evidence found on fouling-up-three habits; estimate league average.
Kept bench players involved late in 2026 playoff games ('anti-Thibs'), rather than collapsing to a six-man clutch unit.
Brown is intensely focused on officiating (laptop press conferences, two Last Two Minute Report grievances in SAC), but no aggregate challenge success-rate data was found.
Warriors-trained, analytics-forward staff; no direct evidence on 2-for-1 hunting (inferred).
No documented pattern of going for the win vs playing for OT; Sacramento late-game choices were criticized more for execution than for risk profile (inferred).
Fired in Sacramento after five straight one-possession losses (Dec 2024) and repeatedly blamed officiating in close games; SI (2026) framed the playoffs as a chance to 'slay his playoff demons'.
Rehabilitated by the 2026 title run (+221 through 12 playoff games), where close-game execution was rarely the story.
SI (2026): Brown 'deserves credit for pulling an anti-Thibs', making tactical adjustments vs Atlanta where Thibodeau 'was more rigid'; Knicks turned the series after a Game 1 loss.
Kings-era criticism: slow to adjust in the 2023 Warriors series (Sabonis-Looney rebounding mismatch) and defensive rigidity.
De'Aaron Fox became an All-Star and Clutch Player of the Year and Sabonis All-NBA under Brown; Keegan Murray set the rookie 3PM record; in NYK, McBride and Shamet expanded roles.
Knicks' young draftees saw limited development minutes during the title push.
Took the Knicks from 28th to 1st in 3PA rate in one season and modernized a bottom-eight passing offense; Kings' record ORtg was built on pace, threes and quick decisions.
Uses film and tracking data publicly to argue officiating and strategy.
Two Coach of the Year awards (2009, 2023) and the 2026 NBA championship in his first Knicks season; SNY report card graded Brown highly after the title.
Detractors note his Sacramento firing and the talent he inherited; some called the hire 'a huge mistake' before the season.

key_criticisms: Sacramento tenure ended with a bottom-half defense, repeated officiating fines ($50K Jan 2024, $35K Nov 2024) and a firing after five straight one-possession losses.
Knicks players were reported midseason (Jan 2026) as still not adjusting to his tactics; Towns struggled with his new offensive and defensive roles.
Bench lineups without a primary ball handler and lineup experimentation drew criticism during the 2026 playoffs.
Pace ambitions only partially realized in New York (bottom-10 early; 20th by season's end).
key_strengths: 2026 NBA champion and two-time Coach of the Year; proven ability to modernize an offense quickly (Knicks 28th to 1st in 3PA rate; record Kings ORtg).
Multi-scheme defense (drop, at-the-level, switch, zone, box-and-one) with a strong defensive coordinator structure.
Deeper, more balanced rotations than his predecessor, keeping stars fresher for the playoffs.
In-series adaptability credited in the 2026 run; strong Warriors/Spurs pedigree in film and preparation.
research_notes: Knicks 2025-26 (53-29, 3rd in East, NBA champions, Finals 4-1 over San Antonio) is consistent across Wikipedia-derived pages and a June 2026 SNY report card, but only one source gave the Finals score. The conference-finals opponent (Cleveland) is inferred from bracket logic (Detroit lost its R2 Game 7 to Cleveland; Knicks swept Philadelphia in R2) and the series score was not found. Sacramento records (48-34, 46-36, 13-18) and prior Cavaliers/Lakers records are from background knowledge consistent with search snippets. The 2026-27 opening record was not retrievable before the search budget was exhausted. Full-season 2025-26 minutes data (Brunson, bench) was not available; depth/minutes scores rest on opening-month reporting plus playoff commentary. Drop-vs-level coverage frequency is contested between sources (Shax says mostly higher coverages; a Jan 2026 blog describes Towns often in drop). No challenge success-rate, fouling-up-three or 2-for-1 data found. Foul discipline, offensive rebounding, risk appetite and two-for-one scores are inferred with confidence <= 0.3.
